title: Quantization Profile Runtime Integration — Scratchpad (lookup/caching/edge cases)
content:
Doc intent: runtime team scratchpad. This is NOT a polished design spec. Captures open questions + decisions as we implement profile resolution + caching in the serving runtime.

Context / what we’re integrating
- Quantization Profile Library = Redwood-published artifacts in model registry (manifest + binaries/weights + kernel constraints + calibration notes).
- Runtime needs to:
  1) Resolve “should we use quantized path?” per request (consider route policy + customer/org overrides)
  2) Fetch profile artifacts (and verify integrity) efficiently
  3) Choose compatible kernel path (GPU arch, driver/CUDA constraints, seq-len regime, model family)
  4) Fall back safely to baseline fp16/bf16 when anything doesn’t line up

Non-goals (runtime)
- Runtime does NOT decide policy. It consumes a “quantization decision”/policy result from routing/control-plane and applies profile selection/compat checks.
- Runtime does NOT accept arbitrary customer-uploaded profiles (v1).

Glossary (for runtime code)
- Profile: quantization artifact + metadata (id, semver, constraints)
- Baseline: non-quantized variant (fp16/bf16 depending on model)
- Execution mode tag: baseline | quantized
- Profile ref: (profile_id, version) OR “latest compatible” pointer depending on policy setting

Assumptions / inputs to runtime
- Request arrives with resolved target model (model_id + model_version) + route_id + org_id + customer_id (tenant)
- Routing/policy engine may attach a quantization directive:
  - disabled
  - enabled: with canary % gating already applied OR directive includes canary % and runtime applies randomization (TBD; prefer policy does it)
  - optional: requested profile ref (pin) OR “allow best compatible profile”
- Runtime also knows hardware context:
  - node gpu_arch (e.g., sm80/sm90)
  - gpu_model (A100/H100/L40S etc.) (useful for perf heuristics)
  - driver/cuda runtime version (major/minor)
  - kernel build version(s)

High-level resolution flow (target state)
1) Parse quantization directive from request context (from router). If missing => treat as disabled for safety.
2) Determine desired profile selection strategy:
   - pinned (id+version)
   - “best compatible” (id fixed, version flexible)
   - “any compatible for model family” (avoid in v1; too risky)
3) Retrieve profile manifest from registry (cached).
4) Run compatibility checks:
   - Model match (model_id / architecture / hidden size / vocab? depending on schema)
   - Hardware scoping match (gpu_arch allowlist/denylist)
   - Kernel constraints (supported kernel family/version)
   - Max sequence length / context window constraints (if profile calibrated only up to N tokens)
   - Quantization format constraints (int8/int4) supported by runtime build
5) If compatible => ensure required artifacts are present locally (download if needed; cache on disk).
6) Select quantized kernel path and execute.
7) Emit metrics tags: profile_id, profile_version, quant_mode(int8/int4), compat_result, fallback_reason (if any).
8) If any step fails => baseline execution + log structured event.

Where to do canary
- Prefer policy engine does canary (route-level toggle). Runtime should be deterministic for same request.
- If runtime must do canary (fallback plan):
  - Use stable hash of (request_id OR trace_id) rather than RNG to avoid per-retry flipping.
  - But request_id not always present. Trace_id is present. Use (trace_id, route_id) -> [0..99].
  - Note: retries might get new trace_id depending on gateway. So still imperfect.
- Action item: align with platform/policy team. For now assume policy attaches “quantization_enabled=true/false” after canary.

Caching strategy (in-memory + disk)
We need to avoid:
- per-request registry calls
- thundering herd when profiles update
- leaking artifacts across incompatible runtime builds
- cross-tenant correctness issues (policies differ by org/customer/route; artifacts can be shared but selection must be per-tenant)

Cache layers
A) Manifest cache (small JSON)
- Key: (profile_id, version) OR (profile_id, “latest”) if we support moving pointer.
- Value: manifest + parsed constraints + resolved artifact URIs + etag/sha256.
- TTL: short (e.g., 60s) for “latest” pointer; long (hours) for pinned versions.
- Invalidation: on registry “profile version changed” event OR if manifest fetch returns new etag.
- Concern: “latest” semantics are tricky. Recommend we do not use “latest” in runtime; policy should pin to an explicit version after approval. If policy wants auto-upgrade, it can do version resolution server-side and pass explicit version down.

B) Artifact presence cache (on-disk)
- Artifacts are bigger (quantized weights, calibration tables, kernel params).
- Store under a content-addressed directory, not tenant-specific.
  - Proposed layout: /var/cache/redwood/profiles/<profile_id>/<version>/<sha256>/...
  - Validate sha256 after download.
- Maintain a local index file to avoid stat-ing many files each request (or use a small in-memory map keyed by (profile_id, version, sha256)).
- Eviction: LRU with size cap per node (configurable). Need to coordinate with other model caches.

C) Compiled kernel / engine cache
- Some quant paths require building/loading a specialized engine. Cache keyed by:
  - model_id + model_version
  - profile_id + profile_version
  - gpu_arch
  - runtime_build_id (critical!)
  - kernel_config (batching/seq-len bins)
- IMPORTANT: if runtime build changes, invalidate compiled engines. (Observed issue in eng-runtime thread 1730894401: mismatch after kernel update.)

Multi-tenant cache keys (edge case)
- Artifacts themselves can be shared across tenants (they’re Redwood-published and identical).
- BUT we cannot cache “decision results” across tenants.
- Split caches:
  - global caches: manifest + artifacts + compiled engines
  - per-tenant or per-route caches: policy decision (if runtime ever computes canary) and maybe “allowed profile list” (but again prefer not in runtime)
- If we introduce any per-tenant caching, key must include org_id + customer_id + route_id + model_id + profile_id. Avoid accidental “quant enabled” leaking to other tenant.

Warmup / prefetch
Goal: avoid first-request penalty when enabling quantization on a route.
Options:
1) Control plane triggers warmup job
- When route toggle enabled (or canary increased), emit event to runtime fleet to prefetch manifest + artifacts.
- This is clean but requires infra.

2) Lazy warmup on first request (v1 likely)
- First request sees directive enabled; we attempt fetch+download; if slow, we can:
  - block and pay latency once (bad for interactive routes)
  - OR temporarily fall back to baseline for that request while warmup happens async (preferred)

Proposed v1 behavior
- If artifacts missing: kick off async fetch; execute baseline for current request; emit metric quant_warmup_in_progress=1.
- Once download completes, subsequent requests can use quant path.
- Add a “min_ready_percent” guard? (not now)

Warmup race / stampede
- Many workers on node see missing artifacts and start downloading simultaneously.
- Need a per-node lock or singleflight mechanism.
- PR 28925 hotfix mentions cache stampede; replicate pattern here:
  - singleflight per (profile_id, version, sha256)
  - exponential backoff when registry/objstore returns 429/5xx

Compatibility checks — details
Hard rejects (must fall back)
- gpu_arch not in allowed list
- runtime_build_id not in supported list (if schema supports)
- kernel family mismatch (e.g., profile requires “rwq_kernels>=1.8” but node has 1.7)
- requested context length > profile.max_context_tokens (if specified)
- model signature mismatch (embedding dims / attention heads etc.)

Soft rejects (can proceed but warn?)
- Sequence length regime mismatch (profile says calibrated for short context only; request is long). I think this should be hard reject unless we can prove safety.
- Tool/JSON mode: runtime can’t detect semantics. That’s eval layer. Not runtime.

Where do we get request sequence length?
- We know prompt token count at runtime (tokenizer output) + requested max_tokens.
- Use worst-case total_tokens = prompt_tokens + max_tokens.

Long-context edge case
- Observed perf regression in long-context workloads when int8 enabled in early tests (see eng-runtime thread 1731012277).
- Hypothesis: kv-cache layout / kernel selection fallback to non-optimal path.
- Runtime should record seq-len bin in metrics and allow profile constraints to specify supported bins.

Fallback behavior / error handling
- Principle: never hard-fail request because quantization profile path fails (unless user explicitly requests it and says “no fallback”, which we are not shipping in v1).
- Fallback reasons to tag:
  - disabled_by_policy
  - manifest_fetch_error
  - manifest_parse_error
  - signature_verification_failed
  - incompat_gpu_arch
  - incompat_kernel_version
  - incompat_model_signature
  - artifacts_missing_warmup
  - artifact_download_error
  - engine_build_error
  - runtime_exception_quant_path

Observability requirements (what we need for triage)
- Log a structured event when directive enabled but we fall back, including:
  - model_id, model_version
  - profile_id, profile_version (if known)
  - node gpu_arch, kernel_version, runtime_build
  - fallback_reason
  - route_id + org/customer ids (hashed?) per privacy rules
- Metrics:
  - quantization_execution_mode{route_id, model_id, profile_id, gpu_arch}
  - quantization_fallback_total{reason}
  - quantization_warmup_latency_ms
  - quantization_manifest_cache_hit_ratio
  - quantization_artifact_cache_hit_ratio

Security / integrity notes (runtime-side)
- Runtime must verify signature/sha256 of manifest and/or artifacts per threat model (see security doc). For now: sha256 check mandatory; signature verification if library supports it in v1 runtime build.
- Ensure artifact download path is least-privilege and doesn’t allow arbitrary URL fetch.

Open questions (need follow-up)
1) Who resolves profile version? Policy layer vs runtime.
   - Strong preference: policy resolves to explicit (profile_id, version) so runtime does not chase “latest”.
2) Do we allow multiple profiles per model (e.g., int8 and int4) and let runtime pick based on seq-len/hw?
   - v1: policy chooses quant mode (int8 vs int4) via profile_id; runtime only checks compatibility.
3) What’s the “model signature” used for compatibility? Need something stable.
   - Suggest: model_id + model_version + architecture + hidden_size + n_layers + n_heads + vocab_size (+ rope type?)
   - Ask Quentin H. what registry already exposes.
4) Shared disk cache location in Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
   - Hosted: local NVMe ok.
   - Dedicated: tenant isolation? still ok since artifacts are Redwood-owned, but confirm.
   - Private: may need configurable cache directory and offline artifact bundle.

Implementation notes / TODO checklist (runtime)
- [ ] Define internal ProfileRef struct: {profile_id, version, sha256, constraints_summary}
- [ ] Implement manifest fetch client with caching + etag handling
- [ ] Add singleflight for manifest fetch and artifact download
- [ ] Add disk cache manager w/ LRU cap + metrics
- [ ] Implement compat checker module; produce typed fallback_reason
- [ ] Wire into model executor selection: baseline executor vs quant executor
- [ ] Add async warmup path (non-blocking) with bounded concurrency
- [ ] Ensure all fallback paths still emit correct billing/cost attribution tags (coordinate w/ Logan/Nadia)

Notes to self (random)
- Make sure cache keys include runtime_build_id; we got burned by this before on engine caching.
- Be careful about “profile enabled” on route but node incapable -> should NOT cause oscillation; we should stick to baseline and report incompat.
- Prefer monotonic safety: adding a new profile should never reduce baseline availability.

Quick links
- ENG-18437 runtime fetch/cache + compat checks
- PR 28766 initial fetch+cache
- PR 28805 fallback semantics
- PR 28925 stampede hotfix pattern (singleflight/backoff)

End of scratchpad (for now).
